title: Nottingham Forest hopeful for Chris Wood return in April after knee injury
content:
Nottingham Forest hope that Chris Wood could return for the final games of their Premier League run-in.

The striker has been sidelined since October with a troublesome knee problem that eventually required surgery to repair at Christmas.

While there remains a mood of caution at the club as Wood continues his recovery, sources close to the forward’s situation say it is hoped that the 34-year-old could — if he does not suffer any further issues along the way — be involved at some point in April.

The New Zealand international was last involved in a 3-0 defeat to Chelsea, in what proved to be Ange Postecoglou’s final game in charge.

He did not play a game under Sean Dyche’s tenure but it would be a major boost for head coach Vitor Pereira to have last season’s 20-goal scorer back available.

Forest have appointed former Tottenham Hotspur head of medicine and sports science Geoff Scott to help address the club’s injury issues.

Although the only other key figure to be missing for any significant period of time this season was Ola Aina who, like Wood, was injured while on international duty. He returned from his hamstring problem in January.

Scott — who is expected to take on the title of head of performance at Forest — worked at Tottenham for two decades, but left during Postecoglou’s tenure in north London.

Forest face Wood’s former club Burnley at the City Ground on April 18, before games against Sunderland (away), Chelsea (away), Newcastle United (home), Manchester United (away) and Bournemouth (home), as they look to avoid the relegation zone.

“I hope he recovers as soon as possible, because he is very important for us,” said Pereira in his press conference ahead of the trip to face Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday. I do not know exactly when he can return. But the information I am being given is that he is working hard to recover as soon as possible.”

Wood is New Zealand’s top scorer with 45 goals, nine of which were scored in their successful World Cup qualification campaign ahead of this summer’s tournament.

Forest might have an issue in goal, with Stefan Ortega having picked up a minor calf problem in the 2-1 defeat to Fenerbahce, as his side progressed into the last-16 of the Europa League with a 4-2 aggregate win last night. On Thursday they drew FC Midtjylland in the next round of the competition.

The former Manchester City player will be assessed, with regular number one Matz Sels expected to return to training on Monday after a groin issue. Angus Gunn, who has made one substitute appearance since joining on a free transfer from Norwich last summer, would be the logical deputy.
